newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks to open lower, slim turnover seen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks to open lower, slim turnover seen.

text.p: After flirting with a record closing high yesterday afternoon, U.S. stocks were expected to open slightly lower, with technology stocks in question after software giant Computer Associates Inc forecast disappointing third quarter revenues.

The Dow Jones Industrial index closed up 24 points to nearly 6547, just more than a point below its all-time closing high record of 6547.79. The Standard & Poor's 500 Index also neared its all-time high finish.

"We may go lower at the opening, but I don't know if we will stay lower. The opening is going to be completely immaterial to how we close," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst for Prudential Securities.
The March futures index of the Standard & Poor's 500 Index, often an indicator of the tenor of the opening for U.S. stocks, fell 1 point to 763.6.
The long bond was up 4/32 to yield 6.58 percent.
